question: The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana was started during the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eighth Five Year Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana (PMRY) was launched on 2 October 1993 during the Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97) to provide self-employment opportunities to educated unemployed youth. (प्रधानमंत्री रोजगार योजना — आठवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• It aimed to assist eligible educated unemployed youth (aged 18-35 years) in setting up self-employment ventures in industry, services and business sectors.

 

• The scheme covered both rural and urban areas, and was later merged into the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) in 2008, along with the Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97) also marked the beginning of economic liberalisation in India and focused on human resource development.

 

NOTE

 

• Ninth Five Year Plan (Option 1): 1997-2002, themed "Growth with Social Justice and Equality."

 

• Seventh Five Year Plan (Option 3): 1985-90, focused on food, work and productivity.

 

• Tenth Five Year Plan (Option 4): 2002-07, aimed at 8% GDP growth.

question: Banganga festival takes place annually at which of the following places in Maharashtra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Banganga Festival is a two-day annual classical music festival held every January at the Banganga Tank, Walkeshwar, Mumbai, Maharashtra. (बाणगंगा उत्सव — मुंबई)

 

• It is organised by the Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation (MTDC) around the ancient Banganga Tank, which is believed to be linked to Lord Rama.

 

• The festival showcases performances by renowned Hindustani classical vocalists and instrumentalists against the backdrop of the historic tank and Walkeshwar Temple.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Banganga Tank is part of the Walkeshwar Temple complex, one of the oldest structures in Mumbai, believed to date back to around 1127 AD.

 

NOTE

 

• Pune (Option 1), Nashik (Option 2) and Nagpur (Option 4): Major cities of Maharashtra, but none of them hosts the Banganga festival.

question: Who was the first social reformer to view modern education as a vehicle for the spread of modern ideas in the country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy, known as the "Father of Modern India"/"Father of the Indian Renaissance," was the first social reformer to view modern Western education as a means of spreading modern, rational ideas in the country. (राजा राम मोहन राय — भारतीय पुनर्जागरण के जनक)

 

• He founded the Anglo-Hindu School (1817) and supported David Hare in establishing the Hindu College, Calcutta (1817), promoting English/Western education.

 

• He founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828 (later the Brahmo Samaj) to reform Hindu society and campaigned against practices such as Sati.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• He was also associated with the Atmiya Sabha (1815) and his campaign against Sati contributed to its abolition through the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829, under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.

 

NOTE

 

• DK Karve (Option 2): Pioneer of women's education and widow remarriage; founded the SNDT Women's University.

 

• Savitribai Phule (Option 3): India's first female teacher; worked for women's education and against caste discrimination.

 

• Swami Vivekananda (Option 4): Propagated Vedanta philosophy and represented Hinduism at the 1893 Parliament of Religions in Chicago.

question: The Mana Ooru - Mana Badi programme was formally launched by the ________ government in March 2022 to introduce English medium in government schools.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Telangana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "Mana Ooru-Mana Badi" (Our Village-Our School) programme was formally launched by the Telangana government in March 2022 to introduce English-medium education and upgrade infrastructure in government schools. (हमारा गांव-हमारा स्कूल — तेलंगाना)

 

• The scheme was launched under Chief Minister K. Chandrashekar Rao (KCR) and aimed at converting government schools into English-medium institutions along with providing corpus funds for infrastructure development.

 

• It sought to improve enrolment and the overall quality of government school education across Telangana.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Telangana also runs residential school networks such as the Telangana Social Welfare Residential Educational Institutions Society (TSWREIS) for disadvantaged students.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 1): Runs the "Ama School" (Mo School) initiative for adopting and upgrading government schools, not this scheme.

 

• West Bengal (Option 2): Not associated with the Mana Ooru-Mana Badi programme.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Runs its own, separately named "Nadu-Nedu" school infrastructure programme, distinct from Telangana's Mana Ooru-Mana Badi.

question: Which of the following is used to chemically test starch?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iodine solution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Iodine solution (iodine dissolved in potassium iodide, i.e. Lugol's iodine) is used to chemically test for the presence of starch; it turns starch a deep blue-black colour. (आयोडीन विलयन — स्टार्च परीक्षण)

 

• This is called the iodine test, based on the formation of a starch-iodine complex where iodine molecules get trapped within the helical structure of amylose.

 

• It is a common qualitative test used in biology and chemistry laboratories to detect starch in food samples, such as potato or bread.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Benedict's solution and Fehling's solution are used to test for reducing sugars (e.g. glucose), turning brick-red on heating.

 

NOTE

 

• Chlorine solution (Option 1): Used as a bleaching/disinfecting agent, not a starch test.

 

• Sulphur solution (Option 3) and Bromine solution (Option 4): Not used for starch testing; bromine water is instead used to test for unsaturation in organic compounds.

question:
Which of the following is the correct match of the column-A with column-B?

Column-A (Nutrients)          Column-B (Source)

i. Protein rich food          a. Wheat

ii. Fat rich food             b. Lemon

iii. Carbohydrate rich food   c. Egg white

iv. Vitamin C rich food       d. Butter and cheese
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-c, ii-d, iii-a, iv-b.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Egg white/egg albumin is a classic protein-rich food (i-c); butter and cheese are rich in fat (ii-d); wheat is rich in carbohydrates (iii-a); and lemon is rich in Vitamin C (iv-b). (पोषक तत्व — स्रोत मिलान)

 

• Proteins are essential for the growth and repair of tissues; egg white (albumin) is almost pure protein.

 

• Fats/lipids are concentrated energy sources; butter and cheese, being dairy-derived, are rich in saturated fats.

 

• Carbohydrates, the primary energy source for the body, are abundant in cereals such as wheat and rice, while Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is abundant in citrus fruits such as lemon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vitamin C is water-soluble, acts as an antioxidant, and also aids iron absorption in the body; its deficiency causes scurvy.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4: Each presents at least one incorrect pairing that mismatches a nutrient with the wrong source.

question: Who was the first Odissi dancer from Odisha to receive Padma Vibhushan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kelucharan Mohapatra was the first Odissi dancer from Odisha to be awarded the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian honour, in the year 2000. (केलुचरण महापात्र — पद्म विभूषण)

 

• He is widely regarded as one of the greatest gurus of Odissi dance, credited with reviving and reconstructing the classical dance form into its present shape in the 20th century.

 

• He trained several eminent dancers, including Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi and Madhavi Mudgal, and earlier received the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan before the Padma Vibhushan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• He also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and gave numerous international performances that helped popularise Odissi worldwide.

 

NOTE

 

• Sonal Mansingh (Option 1): Eminent Odissi and Bharatanatyam dancer awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2003, but she is not from Odisha.

 

• Sanjukta Panigrahi (Option 2): Renowned Odissi dancer and disciple of Kelucharan Mohapatra, awarded the Padma Bhushan, not the Padma Vibhushan.

 

• Madhvi Mudgal (Option 4): Well-known Odissi dancer awarded the Padma Shri, not the Padma Vibhushan.

question: In which state is the Maski inscription located at present?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Maski inscription, discovered in 1915 by C. Beadon, is a Minor Rock Edict of Emperor Ashoka, located at Maski, Raichur district, Karnataka. (मस्की अभिलेख — कर्नाटक)

 

• It is historically significant because it is the only edict that explicitly names "Devanampiya Ashoka," confirming that the emperor referred to elsewhere as "Devanampiya Piyadasi" was indeed Ashoka.

 

• The inscription was crucial in linking the Piyadasi edicts found across India to the Mauryan emperor Ashoka.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Minor Rock Edicts of Ashoka are found at Brahmagiri, Gavimath and Palkigundu (all in Karnataka) and at Bairat (Rajasthan), among other sites.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1), Andhra Pradesh (Option 2) and Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Contain other Ashokan/Mauryan sites, but not the Maski inscription.

question: When did the Drafting Committee publish the first draft of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is February 1948.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly, chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, published the first draft of the Indian Constitution in February 1948. (मसौदा समिति — फरवरी 1948)

 

• The Drafting Committee was constituted on 29 August 1947 and comprised seven members, with Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as its Chairman.

 

• After the first draft was published and circulated for public discussion, a revised draft incorporating amendments was presented in October 1948.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Constitution of India was finally adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950.

 

NOTE

 

• June 1948 (Option 1), May 1948 (Option 2) and January 1948 (Option 3): Incorrect dates; the first draft was actually published in February 1948.

question: Identify the subsidiary of SAIL that is located along the Kolkata-Asansol railway line?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Iron and Steel Company (IISCO).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Iron and Steel Company (IISCO), a subsidiary of Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), is located at Burnpur, near Asansol, along the Kolkata-Asansol railway line in West Bengal. (भारतीय लोहा एवं इस्पात कंपनी — आसनसोल)

 

• IISCO was established in 1918, nationalised in 1972, and later became a subsidiary of SAIL, being renamed IISCO Steel Plant.

 

• Other major SAIL plants are located at Bhilai (Chhattisgarh), Durgapur (West Bengal), Rourkela (Odisha) and Bokaro (Jharkhand).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• SAIL was established in 1954 and is headquartered in New Delhi; it is one of India's largest steel-producing public sector companies.

 

NOTE

 

• ESL Steel Limited (Option 1): Based in Jharkhand and part of the Vedanta Group, not a SAIL subsidiary.

 

• Jindal Steel and Power Ltd (Option 2): A private company, unrelated to SAIL.

 

• Tata Iron and Steel Plant/TISCO (Option 4): Now Tata Steel, located at Jamshedpur, Jharkhand, not a SAIL subsidiary.

question: Name the French jeweller who travelled to India at least six times during the Mughal period.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jean-Baptiste Tavernier.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jean-Baptiste Tavernier, a French gem merchant and traveller, visited India at least six times during the 17th century, during the Mughal period. (ज्यां-बैप्टिस्ट तैवर्नियर — फ्रांसीसी जौहरी)

 

• He is famous for his book "Les Six Voyages de Jean-Baptiste Tavernier" (The Six Voyages), documenting his travels and observations of Mughal India, including the courts of Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb.

 

• He is also credited with acquiring and later selling the famous Tavernier Blue diamond in India, which was later re-cut to form the Hope Diamond.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable European travellers to Mughal India include François Bernier (French physician) and Niccolao Manucci (Italian traveller).

 

NOTE

 

• Antonio Monserrate (Option 1): A Spanish Jesuit missionary at Akbar's court, author of the "Commentarius."

 

• Seydi Ali Reis (Option 3): An Ottoman Turkish admiral and traveller who visited India during Humayun's reign.

 

• Peter Mundy (Option 4): An English traveller and merchant who visited India during Shah Jahan's reign.

question: Which of the following states in India, during October to December, receive rainfall due to Northeast monsoon?
option_1: Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh
option_3: Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka
option_4: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During October to December, the Northeast (retreating) monsoon brings rainfall mainly to Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh, particularly along the southeastern (Coromandel) coast. (पूर्वोत्तर मानसून — तमिलनाडु, केरल, आंध्र प्रदेश)

 

• As the southwest monsoon retreats, the winds reverse direction, blowing from northeast to southwest, picking up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and delivering rain to the southeastern coast of the peninsula.

 

• Tamil Nadu, unusually among Indian states, receives the bulk of its annual rainfall from this Northeast monsoon rather than from the Southwest monsoon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• This retreating monsoon season is also associated with cyclones forming over the Bay of Bengal that frequently affect the eastern coast of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4: List northern/central Indian states (Punjab, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal) that mainly receive rainfall from the Southwest monsoon, not the Northeast monsoon.

question: Machines, tools and implements, and buildings are examples of which type of goods?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Capital goods.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Machines, tools, implements, and buildings used in the production of other goods are examples of Capital goods. (पूंजीगत वस्तुएं — मशीनें व भवन)

 

• Capital goods are durable, man-made goods used as inputs for producing other goods and services, rather than being directly consumed by end users.

 

• They form part of a firm's/economy's fixed capital and are recorded under Gross Fixed Capital Formation in national income accounting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples of capital goods include factory machinery, industrial equipment, commercial buildings and tools used in production.

 

NOTE

 

• Consumer goods (Option 1): Goods directly used/consumed by final consumers, e.g. food, clothing.

 

• Inferior goods (Option 2): Goods whose demand falls as consumer income rises, e.g. low-quality staples.

 

• Intermediate goods (Option 3): Goods used as inputs to produce final goods but themselves consumed/transformed in the process (e.g. steel used to make cars), unlike durable capital goods.

question: Which of the following has the highest value of resistivity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nichrome.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nichrome, an alloy of nickel and chromium, has the highest electrical resistivity among Silver, Nichrome, Chromium and Iron. (निक्रोम — उच्चतम प्रतिरोधकता)

 

• Its high resistivity (about 1.10 × 10⁻⁶ Ωm), combined with a high melting point and resistance to oxidation at high temperatures, makes it ideal for the heating elements of electrical appliances like toasters, heaters and electric irons.

 

• In contrast, silver has the lowest resistivity (about 1.6 × 10⁻⁸ Ωm) among common metals, making it the best conductor of electricity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manganin and constantan are other alloys known for high resistivity and a low temperature coefficient of resistance, used in precision resistors.

 

NOTE

 

• Silver (Option 1): Has the lowest resistivity among common metals, hence the best conductor.

 

• Chromium (Option 3) and Iron (Option 4): Pure metals with moderate resistivity, both lower than that of the alloy Nichrome.

question: Asad Ali Khan is best known for his mastery over which of the given musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rudra Veena.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Asad Ali Khan was an eminent Indian classical musician renowned for his mastery over the Rudra Veena, one of the oldest string instruments in Indian classical music. (असद अली खान — रुद्र वीणा)

 

• He belonged to a tradition closely associated with the Dhrupad style and was one of the last exponents to keep the Rudra Veena tradition alive in modern times.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to Indian classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rudra Veena is a large stringed instrument central to the Dhrupad style of Hindustani classical music, traditionally associated with the worship of Lord Shiva.

 

NOTE

 

• Surbahar (Option 1): A bass sitar-like instrument, associated with artists such as Annapurna Devi, not Asad Ali Khan.

 

• Violin (Option 2): A bowed string instrument; Indian violin maestros include L. Subramaniam.

 

• Tabla (Option 3): A percussion instrument, not associated with Asad Ali Khan.

question: The part of the Himalayas lying between Satluj and ________ rivers is known as Kumaon Himalayas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The part of the Himalayas lying between the Satluj and Kali rivers is known as the Kumaon Himalayas. (कुमाऊं हिमालय — सतलुज और काली नदी)

 

• The Himalayas are longitudinally divided into four regions: the Punjab Himalayas (Indus-Satluj), the Kumaon Himalayas (Satluj-Kali), the Nepal Himalayas (Kali-Teesta), and the Assam Himalayas (Teesta-Brahmaputra).

 

• The Kumaon Himalayas include prominent peaks such as Nanda Devi, Kamet and Trishul, located mainly in the Uttarakhand region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kali river (also called the Sharda/Mahakali) forms part of the India-Nepal border.

 

NOTE

 

• Indus (Option 1): Forms the western boundary of the Punjab Himalayas (with Satluj), not the Kumaon Himalayas.

 

• Brahmaputra (Option 3): Marks the eastern boundary of the Assam Himalayas (with Teesta).

 

• Teesta (Option 4): Separates the Nepal Himalayas from the Assam Himalayas.

question: In December 2021, Aanchal Thakur was in news for winning a bronze medal at an international event. Which sport is she associated with?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alpine Skiing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aanchal Thakur, an Indian alpine skier from Manali, Himachal Pradesh, won a bronze medal in giant slalom at an FIS Alpine Skiing competition held in Kolasin, Montenegro, in December 2021. (आंचल ठाकुर — अल्पाइन स्कीइंग)

 

• She had earlier created history in January 2018 by winning India's first-ever international skiing medal (bronze) at the Alpine Ejder 3200 Cup in Turkey.

 

• With the December 2021 medal, she became the first Indian skier to win two international skiing medals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aanchal Thakur has represented India in international skiing events and is regarded as a pioneering figure for winter sports in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Biathlon (Option 2), Billiards (Option 3) and Figure Skating (Option 4): Different sports, none associated with Aanchal Thakur.

question: Which of the following organisations is credited with writing literary pieces for the abolition of Sati Pratha?
option_1: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>The Harijan Sevak Sangh
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Brahmo Samaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Brahmo Samaj, founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828, is credited with writing literary pieces and campaigning against the practice of Sati Pratha, contributing significantly to its abolition. (ब्रह्म समाज — सती प्रथा उन्मूलन)

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy wrote pamphlets and tracts against Sati and petitioned the British government, which led Governor-General Lord William Bentinck to ban Sati through the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829.

 

• The Brahmo Samaj promoted monotheism, rejected idol worship, and worked against social evils such as Sati, child marriage and rigid caste distinctions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brahmo Samaj later split into factions, including the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj, and influenced later 19th-century reform movements across India.

 

NOTE

 

• The Harijan Sevak Sangh (Option 1): Founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1932, worked for the upliftment of Dalits ("Harijans").

 

• The Satya Shodhak Samaj (Option 3): Founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873, worked against caste discrimination and Brahminical dominance.

 

• The Bahujan Samaj (Option 4): Not a 19th-century reform organisation associated with the Sati abolition movement.

question: The pensions payable to or in respect of the officers and servants of the Supreme Court are charged upon ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Consolidated Fund of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 146(3) of the Constitution, the salaries, allowances and pensions payable to the officers and servants of the Supreme Court are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India. (भारत की संचित निधि — सर्वोच्च न्यायालय पेंशन)

 

• Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is not subject to a vote in Parliament, though it may be discussed.

 

• Similarly, the salaries and pensions of Supreme Court and High Court judges, the President, and the Comptroller and Auditor General are also charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Consolidated Fund of India, established under Article 266, comprises all revenues, loans raised, and repayments received by the Government of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Reserve Bank of India (Option 2): India's central bank, not the source of salaries/pensions of Supreme Court staff.

 

• Public Account of India (Option 3): Holds funds such as provident fund deposits, not judiciary staff pensions.

 

• Finance Commission of India (Option 4): A constitutional body that recommends the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and states, not a fund.

question: On 20 July 2021, the Supreme Court struck down certain provisions of part IX B of the Constitution of India. Part IX B was related to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Co-operative Societies.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 20 July 2021, the Supreme Court (in *Union of India v. Rajendra N. Shah*) struck down key provisions of Part IX-B of the Constitution, which dealt with Co-operative Societies, for want of ratification by at least half the state legislatures. (सहकारी समितियां — भाग IX-B)

 

• Part IX-B was inserted by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011, which sought to promote the democratic, autonomous and professional functioning of cooperative societies.

 

• The Supreme Court held that since cooperative societies fall under the State List (Entry 32), the amendment required ratification by at least one-half of the state legislatures under Article 368(2), which had not been done, and so the provisions applicable to states were struck down.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The provisions of Part IX-B applicable to multi-state cooperative societies (a Union subject) were held valid by the Court.

 

NOTE

 

• Panchayats (Option 1): Governed by Part IX, inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment.

 

• Municipalities (Option 2): Governed by Part IX-A, inserted by the 74th Constitutional Amendment.

 

• Sub-ordinate Courts (Option 4): Governed by Part VI of the Constitution, not Part IX-B.

question: Which of the following Indian states was the host of the 36th national games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gujarat hosted the 36th National Games of India, held from 29 September to 12 October 2022, across six cities: Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot and Bhavnagar. (36वें राष्ट्रीय खेल — गुजरात)

 

• The Games were inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, and featured thousands of athletes competing across numerous disciplines.

 

• The mascot of the 36th National Games was "Savaj," representing the Asiatic lion, symbolic of Gujarat's Gir forest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Host state Gujarat put up its best-ever performance at these National Games, held after a gap caused by the postponement of earlier editions.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1), Maharashtra (Option 2) and Haryana (Option 4): Did not host the 36th National Games; Maharashtra had earlier been slated to host the 34th National Games, which was later shifted to Goa.

question: Which element of Group 17 has two isotopes of masses 35 and 37 amu with average abundance of 75.77% and 24.23%, respectively?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chlorine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chlorine, a Group 17 (halogen) element, occurs naturally as two isotopes: Chlorine-35 (mass 35 amu, abundance 75.77%) and Chlorine-37 (mass 37 amu, abundance 24.23%). (क्लोरीन — समस्थानिक)

 

• The average atomic mass of chlorine, calculated using these isotopic abundances, works out to approximately 35.45 amu, the value listed in the periodic table.

 

• Chlorine is a highly reactive, greenish-yellow gas, widely used in water purification, bleaching, and the manufacture of PVC and other chemicals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Isotopes are atoms of the same element having the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, and hence different mass numbers.

 

NOTE

 

• Iodine (Option 2), Fluorine (Option 3) and Astatine (Option 4): Other Group 17 halogens, but their naturally occurring isotopic compositions differ from the 35/37 amu pair described here.

question: 'Dalkhai' is a folk dance of which of the following states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dalkhai is a popular folk dance of Odisha, particularly performed by communities of the western Odisha region such as Sambalpur, Balangir and Kalahandi. (डालखाई — ओडिशा)

 

• It is performed by women during festivals such as Bhaijiuntia, Nuakhai and Dussehra, often accompanied by traditional instruments like the dhol, nishan and tasha.

 

• The dance depicts themes of love, valour and daily life, and is characterised by rhythmic body movements and vibrant traditional attire.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Odisha include Ghumura and Sambalpuri, alongside the semi-classical Chhau dance.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Known for Bhangra and Giddha.

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Known for Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

question: Which of the following countries never hosted the Paralympic games ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Among Israel, Japan, South Korea and India, India has never hosted the Paralympic Games. (पैरालंपिक खेल — भारत ने कभी मेजबानी नहीं की)

 

• Israel hosted the 1968 Summer Paralympics in Tel Aviv; Japan hosted the 1964 and 2020 (held in 2021) Summer Paralympics in Tokyo; South Korea hosted the 1988 Summer Paralympics in Seoul.

 

• India has participated in the Paralympic Games since 1968 but has never been selected as a host nation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India recorded its best-ever Paralympic performances at the Tokyo 2020 Games, a trend it built on in subsequent editions.

 

NOTE

 

• Israel (Option 1), Japan (Option 2) and South Korea (Option 3): Each has hosted the Summer Paralympic Games at least once, unlike India.

question: The 'Right to Work' plan, under the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, was implemented in how many districts in the first phase?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 200.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Right to Work' plan under the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA), 2005 (now MGNREGA) was implemented in 200 districts during its first phase. (राष्ट्रीय ग्रामीण रोजगार गारंटी अधिनियम — 200 जिले)

 

• NREGA was notified on 2 February 2006 and initially rolled out in 200 of the most backward districts of the country, identified using the Planning Commission's backwardness index.

 

• The Act guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The scheme was extended to 130 additional districts in 2007-08 and covered the entire country by 1 April 2008; it was renamed MGNREGA in 2009.

 

NOTE

 

• 150 (Option 1), 100 (Option 3) and 120 (Option 4): Incorrect figures; the correct number of districts covered in the first phase was 200.
